title: "rush convert"

{{< include ../_setup.qmd >}}

The `convert` command converts between formats without writing an expression.
It reads the input, infers the output format from the file extension (or `-O`),
and writes the result.

## Usage

```bash
rush convert [options] [<file>...]
```

## Basic conversion

```{bash}
rush convert -o penguins.parquet penguins.csv 2>/dev/null
rush run 'nrow(df)' penguins.parquet
```

```{bash}
rush convert -o penguins.json --head 3 penguins.csv 2>/dev/null
cat penguins.json
```

```{bash}
rush convert -O jsonl --head 2 -o penguins.jsonl penguins.csv 2>/dev/null
cat penguins.jsonl
```

## Output templates

Convert multiple files using an output template with yt-dlp-style placeholders:

```{bash}
echo "id,val
1,a
2,b" > chunk1.csv
echo "id,val
3,c
4,d" > chunk2.csv
rush convert -o '%(file_name)s.parquet' chunk1.csv chunk2.csv 2>/dev/null
rush run 'df' chunk1.parquet
```

### Available placeholders

| Placeholder | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| `%(file_name)s` | Input file stem |
| `%(file_index)d` | 1-based file position |
| `%(table_name)s` | Table name (databases) |
| `%(table_index)d` | 1-based table position |

The format spec after `)` follows `sprintf()` conventions: `s` for string, `d`
for integer, `03d` for zero-padded. Use `l` for lowercase or `u` for uppercase:

```bash
rush convert -o '%(table_name)l.csv' sales.duckdb
rush convert -o 'table_%(table_index)03d.csv' big.duckdb
```

## Database output

When the output is a database format (DuckDB or SQLite), multiple inputs become
separate tables named after the input file stems:

```{bash}
echo "id,val
1,a
2,b" > a.csv
echo "id,val
3,c
4,d" > b.csv
rush convert -o combined.duckdb a.csv b.csv 2>/dev/null
rush run 'names(dfs$combined)' combined.duckdb
```

A single input also uses the file name as the table name:

```{bash}
rush convert -o penguins_db.duckdb penguins.csv 2>/dev/null
rush sql "SELECT species, COUNT(*) AS n FROM penguins_db.penguins GROUP BY species" penguins_db.duckdb
rm -f penguins_db.duckdb
```

Convert between database formats:

```{bash}
rush convert -o copy.sqlite shop.duckdb 2>/dev/null
rush run 'names(dfs$copy)' copy.sqlite
```

## Limiting rows

Use `--head` to limit the number of rows written:

```{bash}
rush convert --head 5 -o top5.csv penguins.csv 2>/dev/null
cat top5.csv
```

## Format overrides

Force input and output formats regardless of extension with `-F` and `-O`:

```{bash}
cp penguins.csv penguins.dat
rush convert -F csv -O json -o result.json --head 2 penguins.dat 2>/dev/null
cat result.json
rm -f penguins.dat
```

## Delimiter control

Read a TSV and convert to semicolon-separated CSV:

```{bash}
rush convert --input-delimiter "\t" -D ";" -o cities_semi.csv cities.tsv 2>/dev/null
cat cities_semi.csv
```

## Help

```{bash}
rush convert -h
```

```{bash}
#| include: false
rm -f chunk1.csv chunk2.csv chunk1.parquet chunk2.parquet
rm -f a.csv b.csv combined.duckdb copy.sqlite
rm -f top5.csv result.json cities_semi.csv
rm -f penguins.parquet penguins.json penguins.jsonl
```
